name: Movie global NFO probe collections lifecycle
declaredSeams: Independent fresh roots, fixed English configuration, offline providers, no images/discs/subtitles/lyrics/users/network content. Unused native dependencies fail closed.
Direct real LibraryManager global entry and real Node complete-scan entry; this fixture does not exercise HTTP authorization or a running full native server.

New input preparation clears only the 31 domain tables on a new supplied SQLite byte copy, preserving all DDL, EF tables/history and sqlite_sequence. Preparation is not a native/candidate business operation.

Directory monitoring is a controlled native host boundary. Both media and application-state files are real isolated files. Actual scan, NFO/XML read/save, probe and collection tasks are not substituted.

Both executors receive an already configured empty Movies library via native CollectionFolder.SaveLibraryOptions or the production Node options serializer before the business global scans. No additional candidate-only AddVirtualFolder operation is inserted.

After the created global scan and actual metadata worker drain, both executors explicitly save each declared Movie with MetadataEdit through their actual repository/saver entry point before the stable created snapshot. Local-only global import does not by itself require a Movie NFO saver call. The same two explicit saves, complete events, files and persisted state are required on both sides.

projectionPolicy.rawEvidence: All 33 tables, sqlite_sequence, real XML/NFO, Item events and queue boundaries are saved without projection.
projectionPolicy.itemIdentity: One bijection per run keyed by full native type and declared-root-relative path, or type and exact nonpath name. A stable key must retain its identity across every phase; aliases or changed bindings fail. All foreign keys and declared Data identities use this map.
projectionPolicy.itemValueIdentity: One bijection per run from ItemValueId to exact Type and Value, retained across every phase.
projectionPolicy.paths: Only exact declared case/media/program roots and their descendants map to fixed tokens; no arbitrary drive, temp, or filename deletion. Unknown paths remain literal.
projectionPolicy.clockRules: Ordinary non-minimum clock values must fall within the actual common-input-preparation-to-run-end UTC window. For each logical owner plus named clock field, retain one bijection from distinct actual 100ns values to first-observed-phase tokens across stages and that owner's persisted Data aliases. Nested typed array elements have separate property/index owner roles: a root's VirtualChildren[0].DateLastSaved is not the root's own column clock. Repeated values retain tokens; new values, backwards progression within one role, null and minimum remain distinct. BoxSet DateCreated additionally permits exactly one real ToLocalTime/second-precision XML Added/AssumeUniversal transformation from its actual Added event seed; the seed must lie in the ordinary window, the actual timezone must match the neutral offset, and the actual XML provider must have returned the exact derived value. That transform has its own retained token and never permits repeated timezone shifts. Actual Item event clocks reuse their role bindings and ordered extra tokens for intermediate values. The NFO update separately proves actual DateLastSaved plus >60000ms, without clock override or backdating. Every other Date field remains exact.
projectionPolicy.data: Every Data property is retained; only declared rooted paths, mapped identities and explicitly listed clock properties may be projected. Raw Data text remains in all-table receipts.
projectionPolicy.eventOrder: The entire raw cumulative ordinal stream, including initialization and cleanup, is preserved. Business phase Item events are compared per logical item without dropping multiplicity, order, reasons, Genres, Studios or TmdbCollectionName; setup and close events remain raw diagnostics. Cross-item asynchronous interleaving is diagnostic.
projectionPolicy.postScanTasks: Every native registration must equal the real CoreAppHost exported type order; Node names must match actual task constructor types. In each phase actual task begin/completion sequence must follow that side's registrations. Cross-runtime order equality alone is not required: all persisted/XML/Item-event/queue effects still must agree, and actual differing orders are reported.

queuePolicy.correlation: The two created admissions are actual collection creation and member addition with distinct ForceSave options. Native joins QueueRefresh to RefreshSingleItem by target plus the unmodified DirectoryService reference retained by the real options copy. Candidate matches actual target and effective options, then ALS joins queuedRefresh to metadataScanner. Duplicate semantic signatures or missing starts/completions fail.
queuePolicy.comparison: Compare original per-item request order, effective native option defaults, priority, actual metadata start/completed Item values, failure count, one-to-one admitted/started/completed/drained counts and partial order. Admission-returned may precede or follow start. No positive deduplication input is claimed; every admitted request must execute once.
queuePolicy.completionBoundary: Native has no public full-item queue completion event. The metadata callback is observed directly; full worker completion, including real Folder.ValidateChildren, is acknowledged only after the actual native queue lock reports empty and processing=false. Node additionally saves its real per-item worker completion. The common compared boundary is admitted -> metadata-started -> metadata-completed -> whole-worker-drained. No invented per-item completion timestamp.
queuePolicy.globalReturn: All six raw global-returned/drained snapshots retain 33 tables, actual scan outcome and original queue state. Global-returned snapshots do not open sidecars while real queued savers may own them; files is null at that boundary. Saver observations record real completion without reopening the saved file. Every stable file read after causal real-worker drain must succeed and retains complete original bytes. Success/status is compared at both boundaries; complete persisted state/XML and empty real queue are compared at drained boundaries. Cross-item async interleaving, transient global-returned backlog and caught Native log diagnostics are diagnostic; actual scan failures, per-request partial order, failure/drain obligations and complete drained functional outcomes remain gates.
